column3: Directly repeats conjectural following and fabrication, extending it to majority influence.
Adds that followership can occur without coercive authority, leaving belief and doubt distinct.
Sets divine ownership against the utter lack of possession in those called besides Him.
Immediately reinforces the focus's heavens-and-earth ownership premise and contrasts it with ignorance.
Adds an unwarranted claim about Allah and frames speaking without knowledge as its failure.
Shows shared consequence of association, but adds little about the conjectural route itself.
Explicitly distinguishes following conjecture from knowledge and from what suffices for truth.
Provides a contrasting followed path grounded in insight and cleared of association.
Tests alleged partners by requiring their production, as boundary evidence for unsupported claims.
Restates conjectural following but adds that prevalence does not supply truth.
Adds only the general outcome of fabricating claims about Allah.
Crisis calling to Allah alone exposes the practical collapse of distributed association.
Links inherited names, absent warrant, desire, and conjectural following.
Shows a conjecture becoming socially effective through voluntary following, not proof.
Offers a later recognition of association, but its material setting is indirect here.
Disaggregates alleged partner power into possession, share, and support, denying each.
Connects sole creation and governance with the absence of any other guardian or intercessor.
Makes the called-besides-Allah object incapable of harm or benefit, sharpening the failed route.
Identifies the objects of calling with a rebellious deceiver, but does not develop conjecture.
Its correction of claimed descent is only a channel-level analogy to unsupported naming.
Joins association, inherited excuse, absent knowledge, conjectural following, and fabrication.
Tests partnership by creation, heavenly share, and written warrant rather than asserted promise.
Its mouth-claim versus reality analogy is indirect and already covered by stronger evidence.
Names association a grave injustice, adding an evaluative consequence rather than its mechanism.
Pairs a knowledge-less excuse for worship with fabrication, supporting the focus's epistemic charge.
Supplies the counterpoint of Allah's conclusive proof to conjectural assertions.
Shows renewed association after divine rescue, though the crisis pattern is already established.
Adds the creator/created asymmetry for those invoked besides Allah.
Requires witness while rejecting desire-led following, showing why assertion alone is insufficient.
Bounds any claim to divinity besides Allah by judgment, without addressing the imagined route.
Challenges the naming of partners before the all-knowing overseer and exposes mere outward speech.
At final summons, alleged partners cannot be witnessed; this tests their claimed presence.
Shows damaging assumptions about Allah in distress, only indirectly related to partner-calling.
Directly prohibits calling another deity with Allah, but adds little beyond the basic boundary.
Shows former objects of calling vanishing when no escape remains.
Offers a contrasting response to guidance that excludes associating anyone with the Lord.
Restates that all belongs to Allah and all affairs return to Him.
Makes places of worship exclusively Allah's, directly excluding joint calling.
Contrasts taking another protector with the Creator's self-sufficient provision.
Reinforces comprehensive divine ownership, though it does not address conjectural calling.
States calling the Lord alone and refusing association in the act of calling.
Displays a declared reliance on conjecture rather than certainty, in a different subject matter.
Contrasts the sole Creator with protectors lacking even self-benefit or harm.
Turns an exclusive alliance claim into a test, supporting scrutiny of asserted proximity.
Supplies the adjacent intercessor claim that 10:66 evaluates as unsupported association.
Contrasts following divine guidance with following beings that cannot guide without being guided.
Shows reaction to a servant's sole calling, but not the status of alleged partners.
Shows an assumption about the Lord as ruinous, extending the consequences of false supposition.
Divine praise and mercy here add no clear evidence about association or conjectural following.
Its sufficiency statement is too general to clarify the focus's partner-calling claim.
Names fabricators, but supplies no further relation beyond an already repeated term.
Contrasts steadfastness with following the unknowing, only loosely connected to the focus.
Adds a relational form of association through rival loves despite all power belonging to Allah.
Links following to guidance under divine sovereignty, but is not about asserted partners.
Challenges the attachment of partners to Allah, though the challenge is concise and redundant.
Directly forbids calling what cannot benefit or harm, specifying the practical failure of the route.
Followership and testing occur here without a clear association or conjecture connection.
Its use of calling concerns punishment and contributes no relevant route or claim.
Addresses conduct toward others' objects of calling, not whether their claims are warranted.
Sets Allah's witness and singular deity claim against testimony for other gods.
The spending context gives no material support for the focus.
Tests whether those besides Allah can help or defend, a concise incapacity boundary.
Following satanic steps is not specifically conjectural partner-following.
The final question about claimed partners supplies accountability, but repeats prior summons evidence.
Following the messenger and revealed light do not directly clarify the focus.
Questions assumptions about the Lord, preserving the focus's epistemic concern without partner detail.
Calling to good has no clear relation to calling alleged partners.
Contrasts following revelation with taking protectors besides Allah.
Legal co-ownership is unrelated to alleged divine association.
Denies any protector or helper besides Allah, a secondary boundary on imagined support.
The status of Allah's allies does not address alleged partners or conjecture.
Combines exclusive divine knowledge with no partner in judgment, supporting sole authority.
Its nearness language concerns spending and mercy, not a claimed access route.
The breadth of Noah's call does not clarify partner-calling or conjecture.
Shared heavens-and-earth wording occurs in an unrelated resurrection scene.
Directly describes the structural nonresponse of beings called besides Allah.
Links inherited names without warrant to Allah's exclusive judgment and worship, though later and redundant.
The messenger's call to faith is not evidence about alleged partners.
Explicitly presents alleged protectors as a claimed means of nearness to Allah, directly paralleling f01.
Preserves an alternative inherited path that rejects association, contrasting with inherited unsupported naming.
Restates divine ownership and no other protector, already amply established.
Shows ignorance of scripture accompanied by wishes and conjecture, an epistemic parallel only.
The resurrection scene adds no distinct evidence about association or conjectural following.
Repeats the final question about association without further clarification.
Restates ownership and lack of other support, redundant with earlier cards.
A personal rejection of association adds little after the stronger structural denials.
Denies provision and capability to those worshipped besides Allah.
Reclassifies a prior assumption about claims concerning Allah as unreliable, but without partner-calling.
Exposes resistance to calling Allah alone alongside acceptance of association, directly clarifying the divide.
Calling for destruction in punishment does not bear on the focus.
The earth oath provides no relevant interpretive contribution.
Excludes any protector or intercessor besides Allah at gathering, a secondary route boundary.
Its legal and polemical setting does not clearly illuminate the focus.
Shows a false assumption about Allah's knowledge shaping conduct, an epistemic parallel only.
Its following and harmful learning context is too remote from alleged partners.
Denies any besides-Allah remover, supporting exclusive efficacy without the conjecture element.
Concealing clarification and guidance is not sufficiently connected to the focus.
Crisis produces sincere exclusive devotion to Allah, a nearby lived contrast to imagined access routes.
Counterfactual grief about death does not clarify association or conjectural following.
Its legal association category does not add to the focus's claim about called partners.
Directly joins fabricated partnership claims to speaking about Allah without knowledge.
Rejects an asserted child claim through Allah's creative self-sufficiency, extending the focus's critique of unsupported claims.
Shows people assigning shares to Allah and alleged partners, making association a distributive claim.
Shows alleged partners making a destructive practice appear fair, adding a mechanism of misdirected following.
States undivided worship and the absence of any partner in a concise counterpoint.
Links inherited names lacking authority with the demand for what is asserted through them.
Treats named objects as unsupported designations and awaits the failure of the asserted claim.
Records an inherited-association defense, clarifying how prior generations can be invoked as warrant.
Challenges alleged partners through their inability to create while themselves created.
Adds their inability either to help their callers or to help themselves.
Tests alleged partners by calling them, exposing the claimed parity as ineffective.
Enumerates missing capacities in the objects called besides Allah.
Adds a form of association through conferring lord-like authority on human religious figures.
Provides the immediate eschatological separation between Allah and the partners people claimed.
Makes Allah sufficient witness over the disputed worship relation after that separation.
Forbids worship of what cannot benefit or harm, closely extending the focus's failed-call boundary.
Pairs upright orientation with refusal of association in the same local discourse.
States that no one besides Allah can remove harm or withhold His mercy.
Says the objects called besides Allah brought no benefit and only increased loss.
Contrasts Allah's true call with calls that receive no response, including a vivid unreachable-request boundary.
Frames doubt about Allah against His creative authority over heavens and earth.
Denies Satan any coercive authority and locates the error in response to his call.
Adds that the objects invoked are dead and lack knowledge of resurrection.
Stages the question about alleged partners before those who associated them.
Forbids multiplying deities and commands orientation to the one God.
Forbids constructing likenesses for Allah, bounding speculative comparison.
Links setting another deity with Allah to blame and abandonment.
Invites calling alleged alternatives and denies their power over harm or its removal.
Shows even those invoked seeking nearness to their Lord, undermining their status as access routes.
Shows exclusive calling to Allah at sea when all claimed alternatives disappear.
Denies Allah any partner in dominion and any need of a protector.
Challenges a people who take gods besides Allah to produce clear authority for them.
Shows claimed associates called without response and an uncrossable barrier arising between them.
Closes worship of the Lord to association, supplying a direct positive counterpoint.
Identifies gods taken besides Allah in expectation of honor, exposing a claimed benefit route.
Foresees those gods rejecting their worship and becoming opponents.
Denies a fabricated object power over harm or benefit despite its being treated as a god.
Defines divinity by exclusive knowledge and rejects every other object of worship.
Uses the coherence of heavens and earth to deny the possibility of multiple gods within them.
Requires proof for gods besides Allah and contrasts unsupported assertion with remembrance and revelation.
Challenges whether any gods can protect people from Allah.
Denounces worship without revealed authority or knowledge, directly matching the focus's epistemic critique.
Asks who owns earth and its inhabitants, reinforcing the ownership premise.
Tests claimed protection against the One who protects and cannot be protected against.
Denies child and co-deity claims through the incoherence of competing divine rule.
Denies Allah any partner in dominion and grounds all things in His creation and measure.
Details the inability of gods besides Allah to create, control harm or benefit, death, life, or resurrection.
Questions both the worshippers and those they claimed, exposing the misdirected worship relation.
Repeatedly contrasts Allah with alleged associates in the pattern of rhetorical testing.
Tests association through creation and provision of the heavens-and-earth order.
Tests it through ordering earth, rivers, mountains, and the boundary of seas.
Tests it through response to the distressed caller and removal of harm.
Tests it through guidance in land and sea and provision of winds and rain.
Tests it through origination, return, and provision, then demands proof for the claim.
At final summons, requires claimed partners to answer for their asserted status.
Shows claimed partners summoned and unable to answer, exposing the failed call.
Repeats the final demand to produce the partners that had been claimed.
Forbids calling another god with Allah and grounds exclusive orientation in His enduring judgment.
Explicitly joins worship of idols with fabrication and denies their control of provision.
Portrays taking protectors besides Allah as a fragile reliance, adding an image of failed support.
Tests alleged partners by asking whether they share the provision Allah has given.
Shows people calling Allah sincerely in distress and then associating after mercy.
Requires an authority for association that can speak for the claim, directly testing warrant.
Contrasts Allah's creation, provision, death, and life with associates unable to do any of these.
Questions the angels about whether people worshipped them, testing a possible claimed object.
Records the angels' disavowal and redirects the relation to jinn, preserving an alternative reading of the claim.
States that those called cannot hear or answer, and will deny the association at final reckoning.
Tests taking other gods by their inability to avert intended harm or provide rescue.
Shows gods taken besides Allah in expectation of help.
Denies that those gods can help their worshippers despite the worshippers' service to them.
Challenges worship of objects that people themselves fashion.
Contrasts Allah's creative sovereignty with alleged alternatives unable to remove or withhold what He decrees.
Directly presents the claim of taking intercessors besides Allah.
Locates all intercession with Allah alone, supplying the counterpoint to the intercessor route.
Shows aversion at Allah alone and approval when others are mentioned, clarifying the divided-call response.
Contrasts calling to association without knowledge with calling to the Mighty, Forgiving One.
Rejects worship of those called besides Allah after clear signs, preserving the direct boundary.
Challenges partners alleged to authorize a religion not permitted by Allah.
Shows creatures assigned as a part of Allah, extending unsupported partnership claims.
Demands evidence of creation, heavenly share, or prior record from those associated with Allah.
Shows gods taken for nearness failing to help and disappearing as fabricated association.
Introduces named female deities as a concrete claimed-partner set before the no-authority critique.
Bounds any hoped-for angelic intercession by Allah's permission and approval.
Denies personal control over harm or right guidance, reinforcing exclusive divine efficacy.
Denies any refuge or shelter besides Allah.
